# I. Background

Section 14(a) makes it unlawful to solicit proxies in contravention of the Commission's rules.[^1] The Supreme Court read an implied private right of action into the provision.[^2] Scholars have long questioned that reading.[^3] Later decisions narrowed the right without abandoning it.[^4] The statute itself was never amended.[^5]

[^1]: Securities Exchange Act of 1934 § 14(a), 15 U.S.C. § 78n(a) (2018).
[^2]: J.I. Case Co. v. Borak, 377 U.S. 426, 431 (1964).
[^3]: See Louis Loss, The SEC Proxy Rules in the Courts, 73 Harv. L. Rev. 1041, 1045 (1960).
[^4]: See Borak, supra note 2, at 432; Loss, supra note 3, at 1050.
[^5]: Securities Exchange Act, supra note 1, § 14(a).
